1	\section{The Depth Degradation Atlas}
2	\label{sec:atlas}
3	
4	We present the Depth Degradation Atlas: a systematic empirical map of how statistical fingerprints evolve across recursive generation depths, models, and decoding strategies.
5	The atlas spans $3 \times 3 = 9$ model--strategy cells evaluated at depths $d \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$, with depth extensions to $d{=}5$ for cross-model EDD validation (\S\ref{sec:atlas:edd}).
6	
7	%% ----------------------------------------------------------------
8	\subsection{In-Distribution Performance}
9	\label{sec:atlas:id}
10	
11	Table~\ref{tab:main_matrix} reports four-class Random Forest accuracy (5-fold CV, 200 trees) across all nine cells.
12	Accuracy ranges from 68.9\% (Pythia, top-$k$) to 85.9\% (GPT-2~XL, temperature) four-class (d1--d3 balanced: 58.9--81.5\%), all exceeding the 25\%/33\% chance baselines.
13	Two axis effects emerge.
14	GPT-2~XL achieves the highest accuracy under every strategy (75.8--85.9\%), followed by OLMo (74.4--82.3\%) and Pythia (68.9--78.7\%).
15	Top-$k$ sampling yields the lowest accuracy in every model.
16	The mean within-model strategy gap is 9.3~pp, comparable to the 7.2~pp mean within-strategy model gap; decoding strategy and model family contribute roughly equally to performance variance.
17	
18	\begin{table}[t]
19	\centering
20	\small
21	\caption{Four-class RF accuracy (\%) with bootstrap 95\% CI (${\pm}$half-width; $B{=}1{,}000$). RF with 200 trees, evaluated via 5-fold stratified CV (seed=42). Parenthesized: d1--d3 balanced accuracy from the same 4-class RF (chance = 25\% / 33\%). Depth-0 recall exceeds 97\% in all cells. Within-distribution ordinal quality: MAE\,=\,0.23, QWK\,=\,0.89 (QWK$_{\text{d1--d3}}$\,=\,0.74); 98.2\% of errors fall on adjacent depths ($|\Delta| \leq 1$). $^\dagger$Self-reference scoring (Pythia-1.4B is both generator and reference model); 4--11\,pp advantage over cross-model references (Appendix~\ref{app:ref_ablation}).}
22	\label{tab:main_matrix}
23	\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
24	\begin{tabular}{@{}lccc@{}}
25	\toprule
26	& Nucleus & Temp.\ $\tau{=}0.9$ & Top-$k$ \\
27	\midrule
28	Pythia-1.4B$^\dagger$  & 78.7{\scriptsize$\pm$0.6}\,(71.8) & 76.8{\scriptsize$\pm$0.6}\,(69.3) & 68.9{\scriptsize$\pm$0.6}\,(58.9) \\
29	OLMo-1B     & 78.9{\scriptsize$\pm$0.6}\,(72.7) & 82.3{\scriptsize$\pm$0.5}\,(76.6) & 74.4{\scriptsize$\pm$0.6}\,(66.2) \\
30	GPT-2~XL    & \textbf{84.3}{\scriptsize$\pm$0.5}\,(79.6) & \textbf{85.9}{\scriptsize$\pm$0.4}\,(81.5) & \textbf{75.8}{\scriptsize$\pm$0.6}\,(68.1) \\
31	\bottomrule
32	\end{tabular}}
33	\end{table}
34	
35	\paragraph{Per-class recall.}
36	Depth-0 recall exceeds 97\% in all 9 cells.
37	Among generated depths, d2 consistently yields the lowest recall (44--73\%), followed by d3 (61--80\%) and d1 (72--91\%).
38	The d2 trough reflects its position at the center of the depth gradient, where features overlap with both d1 and d3, consistent with d2-vs-d3 as the EDD bottleneck (\S\ref{sec:atlas:edd}).
39	Full per-class recall appears in Appendix~\ref{app:per_class}.
40	
41	%% ----------------------------------------------------------------
42	\subsection{Feature Consistency Across the Grid}
43	\label{sec:atlas:features}
44	
45	Despite the 17.1~pp accuracy spread across cells, the perplexity tail statistics family (\texttt{p90\_ppl}, \texttt{p75\_ppl}, \texttt{kurtosis\_ppl}) and surprisal variance (\texttt{var\_surprisal}) dominate depth discrimination in every setting.
46	Within this family, \texttt{p90\_ppl} ranks top-2 by Gini importance in all 9 cells and \texttt{var\_surprisal} in 8/9 under SHAP (7/9 Gini; Appendix~\ref{app:permutation}), though individual rankings should be interpreted cautiously given high multicollinearity (VIF${>}$10 for 14--16/19 features).\footnote{The group-level dominance of perplexity tail statistics is robust across importance measures (Gini, SHAP, permutation; Kendall's $W{=}0.90$, $p{<}0.005$).}
47	Table~\ref{tab:feature_importance} shows the full per-cell ranking.
48	
49	Cross-model feature-rank Spearman correlation averages $\bar{\rho} = 0.868$ (range $[0.619, 0.954]$): models agree on which features carry depth information even when they differ in absolute accuracy.
50	Among strategies, top-$k$ yields the highest cross-model rank correlation ($\rho = 0.811$): the deterministic vocabulary truncation imposes a more uniform feature landscape across architectures, at the cost of weaker overall signal (\S\ref{sec:atlas:strategy}).
51	
52	Feature ablation confirms this concentration: the top-5 features achieve 97.6\% of full accuracy (76.5\% vs.\ 78.4\%), with perplexity statistics alone reaching 76.6\% (vs.\ surprisal 73.2\%, other categories ${\leq}$47\%).
53	
54	The feature hierarchy shifts with depth.
55	At shallow boundaries (d1 vs.\ d2), \texttt{var\_surprisal} dominates importance; at deeper boundaries (d3 vs.\ d4, d4 vs.\ d5), tail perplexity statistics (\texttt{p90\_ppl}, \texttt{kurtosis\_ppl}) take over.
56	This transition aligns with model-collapse dynamics~\cite{shumailov2024_nature}: early recursion narrows the surprisal distribution (captured by its variance), while later steps erode the perplexity tail (captured by upper quantiles and kurtosis).
57	
58	\begin{table}[t]
59	\centering
60	\small
61	\caption{Top-5 features by Gini importance. \textbf{Bold}: top-2. \texttt{p90\_ppl} top-2 in 9/9; \texttt{var\_surprisal} 8/9 under SHAP (7/9 under Gini). Individual rankings are approximate due to multicollinearity (VIF${>}$10 for 14--16/19 features).}
62	\label{tab:feature_importance}
63	\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
64	\begin{tabular}{@{}l l@{}}
65	\toprule
66	Cell & Top-5 features (Gini importance, ranked) \\
67	\midrule
68	Pythia, nuc.       & \textbf{var\_surp\,(.17)}, \textbf{p90\_ppl\,(.15)}, m\_ppl\,(.11), var\_ppl\,(.08), p75\,(.07) \\

74	OLMo, nuc.         & \textbf{p90\_ppl\,(.18)}, \textbf{var\_surp\,(.15)}, p75\,(.11), m\_surp\,(.07), ttr\,(.06) \\

76	OLMo, top-$k$      & \textbf{p90\_ppl\,(.20)}, \textbf{var\_surp\,(.17)}, p75\,(.10), m\_surp\,(.07), m\_ppl\,(.05) \\
77	\bottomrule
78	\end{tabular}}
79	\end{table}
80	
81	\begin{figure}[t]
82	\centering
83	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig_atlas_heatmap.pdf}
84	\caption{Atlas feature importance heatmap. Rows: 19 features grouped by category (\S\ref{sec:method:features}); columns: 9 model--strategy cells. Color intensity encodes RF Gini importance. The perplexity-tail and surprisal-variance blocks maintain high importance across all cells.}
85	\label{fig:atlas_heatmap}
86	\end{figure}
87	
88	%% ----------------------------------------------------------------
89	\subsection{Monotonicity and Inter-Depth Distances}
90	\label{sec:atlas:monotonicity}
91	
92	Depth features exhibit strong monotonic trends: perplexity tail statistics decrease with depth (Spearman $\rho = -1.0$ across cell-level medians) while repetition features increase (Figure~\ref{fig:feature_trajectory}).
93	Inter-depth distances are non-uniform: d0-vs-d1 AUC exceeds 0.99 in all 9 cells, whereas d2-vs-d3 ranges from 0.69 to 0.89.
94	
95	% Feature trajectory figure moved to Appendix for space
96	
97	%% ----------------------------------------------------------------
98	\subsection{EDD Analysis}
99	\label{sec:atlas:edd}
100	
101	We extend the benchmark to depth $d{=}5$ for all three models under nucleus sampling.
102	Each model's depth-3 LoRA checkpoint is used to finetune and generate depth-4 data, and the process repeats for depth~5; feature extraction uses the same reference model (Pythia-1.4B).
103	We train dedicated binary RF classifiers (500 trees) for each adjacent pair, as defined in Eq.~\ref{eq:edd}.
104	
105	\paragraph{AUC decay and cross-model convergence.}
106	For Pythia-1.4B (nucleus), AUC decays monotonically from $0.999$ (d0v1) to $0.683$ (d4v5); AUC-excess contraction ratios (0.80 at d1v2$\to$d2v3, 0.69 at d3v4$\to$d4v5) show convergence toward indistinguishability accelerates with depth (Figure~\ref{fig:auc_decay}).
107	The d3-vs-d4 AUC clusters near $T{=}0.75$ for all three models (Pythia $0.784$, OLMo $0.765$, GPT-2~XL $0.750$), while d4-vs-d5 converges to a narrow band ($0.681$--$0.684$, range $0.003$), suggesting an architecture-independent depth ceiling within the 1--1.5B nucleus setting.
108	Bootstrap testing ($H_0{:}\, \mathrm{AUC} \leq 0.75$) yields $p = 0.001$ (Pythia), $0.091$ (OLMo), $0.505$ (GPT-2~XL).
109	
110	\paragraph{EDD threshold sensitivity.}
111	Across the 9-cell benchmark (depths 0--3), all cells achieve $\mathrm{EDD}{=}3$ at $T{=}0.65$; at $T{=}0.70$, 8/9 cells; at $T{=}0.75$, 7/9; at $T{=}0.80$, 5/9.
112	Top-$k$ configurations lose $\mathrm{EDD}{=}3$ first (Pythia top-$k$ at $T{=}0.70$, OLMo top-$k$ at $T{=}0.75$); d2-vs-d3 is the consistent bottleneck.
113	
114	\begin{figure}[t]
115	\centering
116	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig_auc_decay.pdf}
117	\caption{Binary pairwise AUC decay curves for three models (nucleus sampling, depths 0--5). Horizontal dashed lines mark $T \in \{0.65, 0.70, 0.75, 0.80\}$. All three curves converge below 0.70 at d4-vs-d5, while d3-vs-d4 AUC clusters in the range 0.750--0.784. Shaded bands: bootstrap 95\% CIs.}
118	\label{fig:auc_decay}
119	\end{figure}
120	
121	%% ----------------------------------------------------------------
122	\subsection{Strategy-Dependent Trajectories}
123	\label{sec:atlas:strategy}
124	
125	The three strategies induce qualitatively distinct degradation trajectories.
126	Temperature ($\tau{=}0.9$) yields the highest accuracy in 2/3 models (GPT-2~XL 85.9\%, OLMo 82.3\%) because uniform logit scaling accelerates convergence to an attractor~\cite{shumailov2024_nature}, amplifying the fingerprint but creating a boundary reversal risk under cross-strategy transfer (\S\ref{sec:generalization}).
127	Top-$k$ ($k{=}50$) produces the lowest accuracy (68.9--75.8\%) because hard vocabulary truncation removes depth-discriminative low-probability tokens.
128	The strategy effect (9.3\,pp range) exceeds the model effect (7.2\,pp); deployment-time knowledge of the decoding strategy matters at least as much as the generator model.
129

1	\section{Generalization and Robustness}
2	\label{sec:generalization}
3	
4	We test whether atlas accuracy (68.9--85.9\% four-class; d1--d3: 58.9--81.5\%) reflects genuine statistical regularities across eight generalization axes (five below, three in Appendix).
5	
6	\subsection{Classifier Comparison and Surface-Text Ablation}
7	\label{sec:gen:baselines}
8	
9	Table~\ref{tab:baselines} compares ordinal depth estimation methods across all 9 atlas cells.
10	RF, XGBoost, and LightGBM on the same 19 features converge within 0.4\,pp per cell (a feature-determined ceiling); on Pythia nucleus, CORAL \cite{coral2020} (78.1\%) and DivEye \cite{diveye2026} (78.2\%) match RF within 0.6\,pp ($p>0.05$).
11	
12	\paragraph{Neural end-to-end baselines.}
13	DeBERTa-v3-base (LoRA) trained end-to-end on raw text underperforms RF by 16--32\,pp across three cells (Table~\ref{tab:baselines}); the gap is largest on GPT-2~XL temp09 (53.1\% vs.\ 85.9\%), where RF signal is strongest.
14	Depth-2 recall collapses to 8.4\% under DeBERTa, indicating that intermediate-depth distributional shifts---captured by perplexity tail statistics---are invisible to token-level neural encoders without explicit feature engineering.
15	RoBERTa-DCOL (ordinal contrastive; 64.5\%) narrows the gap but remains 14\,pp below RF.
16	
17	\paragraph{Binary detectors and membership inference.}
18	Perturbation-based (DetectGPT, 28.8\%) and membership-inference (Min-K\% Prob, 33.2\%) methods produce scores with no ordinal resolution (Table~\ref{tab:baselines}); CORAL calibration does not close the gap (d1--d3: 40.4\% vs.\ RF 71.6\%).
19	Binoculars \cite{binoculars2024}, calibrated with an 11-feature RF on per-token cross-perplexity scores, matches our pipeline within 0.3\,pp (78.1\% vs.\ 78.4\%, $p{>}0.05$); 6 of 11 Binoculars features overlap with 6 of our 19 (both capture mean-level perplexity displacement), and merging all 30 features yields 82.6\% (+4.2\,pp; Appendix~\ref{app:feature_ablation_bino}).
20	
21	\paragraph{Surface-text ablation.}
22	Single-feature regression on mean perplexity performs at chance (25.1\%); zero-shot LLMs (DeepSeek V3.2, 36.2\%; Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, 30.4\%) also fail (43\,pp below the best RF cell; Appendix~\ref{app:zeroshot_prompt}); depth signal resides in distributional statistics inaccessible from surface text.
23	
24	\begin{table}[t]
25	\centering
26	\small
27	\caption{Ordinal depth estimation: method comparison. RF mean across 9 atlas cells (5-fold CV, 200 trees); DeBERTa-v3 range across 3 tested cells; DetectGPT: 9/9 cells; Binoculars: observer=Pythia-1.4B, performer=Pythia-410M, 9/9 cells. Chance = 25\% (4-class) / 33.3\% (d1--d3).}
28	\label{tab:baselines}
29	\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
30	\begin{tabular}{@{}llcc@{}}
31	\toprule
32	Method & Calibration & 4-Cl (\%) & d1--d3 (\%) \\
33	\midrule
34	RF 19-feature (ours) & RF & \textbf{78.4} & \textbf{71.6} \\
35	Binoculars \cite{binoculars2024} & threshold & 69.8 & --- \\
36	Binoculars \cite{binoculars2024} & RF (1 feat) & 63.7 & --- \\
37	RoBERTa-DCOL (ordinal) & contrastive & 64.5 & --- \\
38	DeBERTa-v3 (end-to-end) & cross-entropy & 53.1--60.6 & --- \\
39	\midrule
40	Zero-shot LLM (best) & --- & 36.2 & --- \\
41	Min-K\% Prob \cite{shi2024_minkprob} & CORAL & 33.2 & 40.4 \\
42	DetectGPT \cite{mitchell2023_detectgpt} & best-of-3 & 28.8 & 24.3 \\
43	Random & --- & 25.0 & 33.3 \\
44	\bottomrule
45	\end{tabular}}
46	\end{table}
47	
48	Convergence confirms the signal resides in the features: three classifiers match within 0.8\,pp (Appendix~\ref{app:learned_estimator}), perplexity features alone recover 66.0\%, and seed replication across three families shows $\Delta{\leq}3.2$\,pp (Appendix~\ref{app:seed_replication}).
49	Figure~\ref{fig:confusion_matrix} shows d0 near-perfectly identified (recall ${>}$99\%); errors concentrate at d2/d3 in-distribution and spread to d1--d3 under transfer.
50	
51	\begin{figure}[t]
52	\centering
53	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig_confusion_matrix.pdf}
54	\caption{Confusion matrices for the best in-distribution setting (GPT-2 XL, temp $\tau{=}0.9$, 85.9\%) and the best cross-model leave-one-out transfer (OLMo holdout, 69.2\%). d0 recall exceeds 99\% in both; errors spread across the d1--d3 range under transfer.}
55	\label{fig:confusion_matrix}
56	\end{figure}
57	
58	\subsection{Cross-Model Transfer}
59	\label{sec:gen:crossmodel}
60	
61	We perform leave-one-model-family-out evaluation: train on two families (nucleus only), test on the held-out third (Table~\ref{tab:cross_model}).
62	
63	\begin{table}[t]
64	\centering
65	\small
66	\caption{Cross-model transfer (leave-one-out, nucleus only). Chance = 25\% / 33\% (d1--d3). d1--d3 bal.\ acc: Pythia 49.9\%, OLMo 59.2\%, GPT-2~XL 57.2\% (mean 55.4\%). Ordinal quality: MAE\,=\,0.39, QWK\,=\,0.81 (QWK$_{\text{d1--d3}}$\,=\,0.53); 94.8\% of errors at $|\Delta| \leq 1$.}
67	\label{tab:cross_model}
68	\begin{tabular}{lccccc}
69	\toprule
70	Holdout & Acc & d0 & d1 & d2 & d3 \\
71	 & (\%) & Rec. & Rec. & Rec. & Rec. \\
72	\midrule
73	Pythia & 62.4 & 100.0 & 49.3 & 26.8 & 73.6 \\
74	OLMo & \textbf{69.2} & 99.3 & 75.5 & 43.3 & 58.8 \\
75	GPT-2 XL & 67.6 & 98.5 & 74.7 & 52.6 & 44.5 \\
76	\midrule
77	Mean & 66.4 & 99.3 & 66.5 & 40.9 & 59.0 \\
78	\bottomrule
79	\end{tabular}
80	\end{table}
81	
82	Mean transfer accuracy is 66.4\% four-class (d1--d3: 55.4\%; $2.7\times$ chance); d0 recall ($>$98\%) inflates the four-class headline, and d2 recall drops to 26.8\% in the worst case (Pythia holdout).
83	
84	\subsection{Cross-Strategy Transfer}
85	\label{sec:gen:crossstrategy}
86	
87	Table~\ref{tab:cross_strategy} reports leave-one-strategy-out transfer.
88	
89	\begin{table}[t]
90	\centering
91	\small
92	\caption{Cross-strategy transfer (leave-one-out). Chance = 25\% / 33\% (d1--d3). d0 recall $\geq$89\% inflates headline; d1--d3 mean: 45.9\%.}
93	\label{tab:cross_strategy}
94	\begin{tabular}{lccc}
95	\toprule
96	Holdout & Pythia & OLMo & GPT-2 XL \\
97	 & Acc (\%) & Acc (\%) & Acc (\%) \\
98	\midrule
99	nucleus & \textbf{69.4} & \textbf{65.4} & \textbf{59.9} \\
100	temp ($\tau{=}0.9$) & 62.8 & 58.2 & 56.1 \\
101	top-$k$ ($k{=}50$) & 51.5 & 54.9 & 53.6 \\
102	\bottomrule
103	\end{tabular}
104	\end{table}
105	
106	Cross-strategy transfer yields 59.1\% four-class (d1--d3: 45.9\%, chance = 33\%), 7\,pp below cross-model transfer.
107	This gap is itself an empirical finding: different decoding strategies induce structurally distinct degradation trajectories in feature space, not merely noisier versions of the same trajectory.
108	Training on nucleus + top-$k$ inverts the d1/d2 boundary under temperature (d1v2 AUC $<$ 0.5), because temperature scaling accelerates convergence (\S\ref{sec:method:theory}).
109	A two-stage pipeline (strategy identification + depth classification) recovers 11.5\,pp, with a 31.5\,pp d1--d3 gap between correct and wrong routing confirming feature-space misalignment (Appendix~\ref{app:extended_discussion}).
110	
111	\paragraph{Prompted generation.}
112	Topic-seeded generation (GPT-2~XL nucleus) yields 69.5\% ($-$13.8\,pp vs.\ BOS-seeded, $2.8{\times}$ chance) with monotonic AUC decay and identical top features (Appendix~\ref{app:prompted_gen}).
113	
114	%% ----------------------------------------------------------------
115	\subsection{Preliminary Cross-Scale Observations}
116	\label{sec:gen:crossscale}
117	
118	Depth signal persists at 14B (Qwen2.5-14B, clean FP16, self-reference) across all three strategies: nucleus 54.1\%, temperature 50.5\%, top-$k$ 47.9\% (mean 50.8\%, $2{\times}$ chance), with strategy-specific AUC patterns confirming trajectory divergence at larger scale (Appendix~\ref{app:cross_scale_full}).
119	Cross-domain arXiv achieves 74.1\% at the primary 1--1.5B scale (Appendix~\ref{app:cross_scale_full}).

Key observations for my review:

## Paper Summary
The paper proposes a method for estimating the recursive generation depth (how many times text has been through a model → train → generate cycle) using statistical fingerprints (primarily perplexity tail features). 

The authors build a 180K benchmark spanning three model families, three decoding strategies, and four depths, demonstrating that a Random Forest classifier using 19 statistical features achieves 68.9-85.9% accuracy across different settings. They also introduce the EDD metric to quantify how distinguishable adjacent depths remain throughout a generation chain.

## Now let me analyze each review dimension:

### 1. 实验设计与统计分析

**Strengths:**
- The 180K benchmark is systematically constructed with careful control over model family, decoding strategy, and depth variables
- Feature engineering is grounded in model collapse theory with clear motivation
- Multiple feature importance measures (Gini, SHAP, permutation) show consistent agreement

**Weaknesses:**
- The LoRA configuration (r=16, α=32) is borrowed directly from prior work without justification for why these values suit recursive chain construction, and no hyperparameter ablations are conducted. While the paper acknowledges this limitation, for claims about intrinsic properties of recursive generation it would strengthen the work to verify the depth signal isn't tied to this specific LoRA setup.

- The Random Forest classifier performs comparably to CORAL and XGBoost within 0.8 percentage points, which suggests the signal comes from the feature representation itself rather than the classifier choice.

- Cross-validation appears sound since different depth samples come from different LoRA checkpoints, though there's a shared-origin effect since all d0 and d1 samples trace back to the same Wikipedia subset.

- Bootstrap confidence intervals and p-values are used correctly throughout, but the curation proof-of-concept lacks multiple comparison corrections—after applying Bonferroni adjustment, only a fraction of the comparisons remain significant.

Now looking at the cross-transfer results: the 66.4% cross-model transfer rate is heavily driven by near-perfect d0 recall, while d1-d3 balanced accuracy sits at just 55.4%, only 1.66× chance level. The Pythia holdout shows d2 recall dropping to 26.8%, which is too low to be practically useful. Cross-strategy transfer at 59.1% is similarly modest—the d1-d3 balanced accuracy of 45.9% is barely above chance at 1.38×, and there's an interesting inversion where d1/d2 discrimination actually performs worse than random under temperature holdout.

The two-stage pipeline's 11.5 percentage point recovery is noteworthy, though it requires advance knowledge of the strategy space. The cross-domain result at 74.1% is somewhat misleading since it's still within the same model and strategy, just using different seed text from arXiv abstracts.

For the EDD metric, the contiguous prefix requirement makes sense for monotonic decay patterns, but the T=0.70 threshold choice lacks strong justification—the paper tests multiple thresholds but doesn't clearly explain why 0.70 is optimal beyond calling it "adequate discrimination." The framework also struggles with non-monotonic cases, particularly in instruction-tuned models.

The core issue is that EDD becomes uninformative when it returns zero, and the contiguous prefix constraint means it can't capture discriminability at deeper levels if the initial threshold fails—like the 14B model where the first comparison falls below 0.70 but later comparisons exceed it.

Comparing against Binoculars reveals the real tension: their method achieves 78.4% versus Binoculars' 78.1%, a difference of just 0.3 percentage points that isn't statistically significant. The paper frames their contribution as the ordinal depth framework rather than raw performance gains, yet the merged system reaching 82.6% suggests the two approaches capture partially complementary signals.

The baseline comparisons also need context—DetectGPT and Min-K% Prob were designed for binary classification, not ordinal depth estimation, so their 28.8% and 33.2% performance gaps are less surprising when adapted through "best-of-3" and ordinal calibration techniques. Similarly, the zero-shot LLM results (DeepSeek V3.2 at 36.2%, Qwen2.5-7B at 30.4%) reflect that these models lack training on identifying recursive generation depth, making the prompt-based approach inherently limited.

The prompt template itself introduces potential bias by providing explicit depth-pattern descriptions rather than letting models infer depth organically. There's also a self-reference issue with Pythia-1.4B serving as both the reference model and one of three generators—it shows a 4-11 percentage point advantage over cross-reference comparisons, with the ablation revealing an 11.3 percentage point spread between Pythia self-reference (78.6%) and GPT-2 XL cross-reference (67.3%). The paper acknowledges this transparently, but it systematically advantages Pythia in the main results. Now looking at the cross-scale experiments with the 7-8B models...

The 7-8B results show Llama-3.1-8B at 70.2% and Qwen2.5-7B at 60.1%, but there are multiple confounds: 4-bit quantization, smaller sample size, nucleus sampling only, and vocabulary mismatch with the reference model. With just two models tested, it's hard to generalize. The 14B results are even more problematic—Qwen2.5-14B reaches 50.8% (above chance) but with EDD=0, meaning no adjacent-depth pair is actually discriminable at the threshold. \section*{Limitations}
\label{sec:limitations}

\paragraph{Full-replacement vs.\ accumulation.}
All experiments use full-replacement recursive chains, where each depth fully replaces the prior training corpus. Real-world contamination typically involves accumulation, where synthetic and human data co-exist at unknown proportions across iterations \cite{gerstgrasser2024_accumulate}. Under accumulation, depth signal should attenuate because each generation retains human-originated distributional properties. Our results therefore represent an upper bound on feature separability; extending the framework to accumulation settings, where depth becomes a continuous mixing parameter, is a priority for future work.
Segment-level estimation in mixed-depth documents remains open (Appendix~\ref{app:mixed_depth}), as our framework assumes uniform depth per passage.

\paragraph{Controlled experimental setting.}
The primary benchmark uses Wikipedia seed text with controlled LoRA fine-tuning (1--1.5B models), a design that isolates the depth variable but diverges from wild contamination.
Domain bias controls confirm depth as the dominant factor: LOGO accuracy (72.1\%) matches standard CV (72.0\%), seed-group prediction is at chance (10.2\%; Appendix~\ref{app:domain_bias}).
Cross-scale experiments (7--14B, \S\ref{sec:gen:crossscale}) show signal that attenuates with scale; at 14B, d0/d1 separability nearly vanishes ($\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}0$) while d1--d3 discrimination persists; this constitutes a boundary condition for the current feature set (confounded by five factors; Appendix~\ref{app:cross_scale_confounds}).

\paragraph{Cross-strategy deployment constraint.}
Cross-strategy transfer induces a d1/d2 boundary inversion under temperature sampling.
Per-strategy z-score normalization partially corrects the inversion under logistic regression (GPT-2~XL d1v2 AUC $0.24{\to}0.56$, OLMo $0.19{\to}0.70$) but yields negligible improvement for the Random Forest ($\Delta < 0.02$\,pp); a two-stage pipeline is needed for reliable cross-strategy deployment.
In strategy-unknown settings, d1--d3 accuracy drops to 45.9\%; the pipeline recovers 11.5\,pp, though gains vary across models (GPT-2~XL $+$16.4\,pp vs.\ Pythia $+$8.0\,pp).

\paragraph{d0 inflation of headline metrics.}
Depth~0 (human-written text) is near-perfectly separable (recall $>$97\%), inflating four-class accuracy.
Cross-model transfer of 66.4\% is substantially driven by d0; d2 recall drops to 26.8\% in the worst case (Pythia holdout).
We report d1--d3 balanced accuracy alongside all four-class headlines to address this inflation.

\paragraph{Domain-dependent false positive rate.}
On editorial text (WikiText-103), all classifiers achieve $\geq$98.5\% d0 accuracy, but on web-crawl data (C4, 5{,}000 passages), per-model FPR ranges from 4.7\% (OLMo) to 22.4\% (GPT-2~XL).
A pooled RF classifier evaluated on larger corpora (10{,}000 passages each) yields 34\% FPR on C4 and 17\% on FineWeb \cite{penedo2024_fineweb}; the gap reflects quality filtering in FineWeb removing feature-anomalous text that triggers false positives.
Misclassifications concentrate in template/SEO content with elevated repetition features (\texttt{rep\_3gram} $+$37\%, \texttt{rep\_4gram} $+$75\% vs.\ correctly classified d0).
Confidence thresholding ($P(\mathrm{d0}) \geq 0.15$) reduces pooled FPR from 34\%/17\% to 2.8\%/0.7\% on C4/FineWeb at minimal accuracy cost ($-$0.3\,pp); high FPR is therefore a decision-threshold problem, not a fundamental calibration defect, though the optimal threshold remains domain-dependent (Appendix~\ref{app:calibration}).

\paragraph{Adversarial robustness.}
Adversarial paraphrasing \cite{sadasivan2023_paraphrase} could disrupt the perplexity tail features that drive classification; depth estimation's robustness under such attacks is untested.

\paragraph{EDD monotonicity assumption.}
Our EDD definition (Eq.~\ref{eq:edd}) requires all pairwise AUCs up to depth $d^*$ to exceed $T$, which is well-behaved when AUC decays monotonically, as observed in all our configurations.
However, \citet{bakshi2026_collapse_improvement} show that early recursion can temporarily \emph{improve} model quality, which could produce non-monotonic AUC profiles (e.g., a dip at d1/d2 followed by recovery at d2/d3).
Our cross-strategy transfer results provide an empirical example: training on nucleus + top-$k$ and testing on temperature yields d1-vs-d2 AUC as low as 0.129 (GPT-2~XL) and 0.253 (OLMo), violating the monotonicity assumption.
In such cases EDD would conservatively report a lower value than the deepest discriminable pair, potentially underestimating the true discriminable range; extending EDD to handle non-contiguous discriminable regions is future work.
The choice of threshold $T$ is also application-dependent: at $T{=}0.80$, several cells lose one depth level relative to $T{=}0.75$.

\paragraph{Reference model dependency.}
Reference model choice affects classification accuracy by up to 11\,pp; same-family references yield optimal performance, though all configurations exceed $2.5\times$ chance.
Surprisal-based features are computed relative to Pythia-1.4B, which coincides with one of the three generators.
For the Pythia pipeline this constitutes self-model feature extraction, while OLMo and GPT-2~XL measurements are cross-model.
The self-reference configuration yields a 4--11\,pp advantage over cross-model references (Table~\ref{tab:ref_ablation}); Pythia results in Table~\ref{tab:main_matrix} ($^\dagger$) should be interpreted with this caveat.
An ablation with OLMo-1B and GPT-2 XL as alternative references shows accuracy ranging from 67--79\% across three reference architectures (Appendix~\ref{app:ref_ablation}), all exceeding $2.5\times$ chance; same-family reference yields optimal performance ($\Delta{\leq}$11\,pp).
The choice of reference model affects feature values; a different reference model may shift absolute feature magnitudes and potentially alter discriminability at depth boundaries.
Reference-free surface features alone achieve 53.7\% (partial signal in lexical statistics) but trail the full pipeline by 25pp; surprisal-based features are therefore essential.
Simple multi-reference ensembling does not outperform the best single reference (73.7\% vs.\ 78.6\%).

\paragraph{Single LoRA instance.}
Cross-seed replication covers 3 of 9 cells (Pythia, OLMo, GPT-2~XL nucleus); seed=43 yields $+$0.1 to $+$3.2\,pp higher accuracy, with 2/3 deltas statistically significant (non-overlapping CIs).
Feature rankings and depth ordering are consistent across seeds, but single-seed absolute accuracy carries ${\sim}$1--3\,pp uncertainty; cross-cell comparisons should be interpreted cautiously.

\paragraph{Additional caveats.}
Depth signal scales with passage length (68.4\% at 128 tokens, 77.8\% at 512; Appendix~\ref{app:length_ablation}), saturating near 500 tokens.
Prompted generation was validated on only 1 of 9 cells (GPT-2~XL nucleus); generalization to other model--strategy configurations under prompted conditions is not established.
Detection features degrade under domain shift \cite{pudasaini2026_detection_fails}, and curated synthetic data may not trigger collapse \cite{falahati2026_curated}, attenuating the fingerprints we exploit.

\section*{Ethics Statement}

This work uses publicly available pretrained language models (Pythia-1.4B, OLMo-1B, GPT-2~XL) and Wikipedia text as seed data.
No human subjects were involved, no private or sensitive data were collected, and no new models were released.
Our method is intended to support data provenance and training-data auditing; we acknowledge that depth estimation tools could in principle be misused to circumvent content moderation, though such risks are shared with all detection-oriented research.
Code and data will be released upon acceptance.
This research used AI coding assistants for experiment implementation and writing drafts.
All scientific decisions, experimental design, and result interpretation were conducted by the authors.

- 问题：d0（human-written）召回率 >97%（Table 2 脚注），four-class accuracy 被 d0 严重拉高。Cross-model transfer 的 66.4% 中 d0 贡献巨大，d1-d3 balanced accuracy 仅 55.4%（1.66× chance）。Pythia holdout d2 recall 仅 26.8%（Table 5）。Abstract 和 Introduction 始终以 four-class accuracy 作为主指标，d1-d3 balanced accuracy 虽有报告但始终处于括号内或脚注位置。这在实际应用中会误导用户：一个能以 97% 识别人类文本但只有 26.8% 识别 d2 的系统，其实用价值与 "66.4% accuracy" 给人的印象截然不同。
- 为什么影响接收：ACL ARR soundness 要求 claims 与 evidence 匹配。当前表述方式让读者高估了方法在真正困难（d1-d3 discriminability）场景下的能力。
- 建议修改方向：(1) Abstract 和 Introduction 同时并列报告 four-class accuracy 和 d1-d3 balanced accuracy；(2) 在 Section 6 Discussion 中明确承认 d0 膨胀效应并量化其影响；(3) 考虑以 d1-d3 balanced accuracy 作为主指标。

**N2** [critical] 与 Binoculars baseline 无显著差异（78.4% vs 78.1%, p>0.05），论文未充分定位自身方法的附加价值
- 具体位置：Section 5.1 Table 4, Section 5.1 正文第 3 段, Appendix B.17 Table B.17
- 问题：论文 19-feature RF（78.4%）与 Binoculars 11-feature RF calibration（78.1%）在 9-cell mean 上无统计显著差异。Table 4 中 Binoculars 行列出的是 threshold（69.8%）和 RF (1 feat)（63.7%）两个较弱配置，78.1% 的完整 11-feature 配置仅在正文中一句话提及。这种呈现方式不透明。Merged 30-feature 达到 82.6%（+4.2pp），说明两个管线的信号部分互补——但互补性本身暗示 19-feature pipeline 并未完全覆盖 Binoculars 的信号，反之亦然。
- 为什么影响接收：如果一个已有方法（Binoculars + RF calibration）已经达到相同性能，那么本文的方法论贡献（19-feature pipeline）需要通过其他维度（如 interpretability、deployment cost、无需 performer model）来论证，而非仅以 accuracy 定位。
- 建议修改方向：(1) Table 4 中加入 Binoculars 11-feat RF 行并标注 p-value；(2) 明确论证本文管线相对 Binoculars 的优势（如单一 reference model 即可、无需 observer-performer pair、特征可解释性、merged system 的增益来源）；(3) 将 merged 82.6% 作为推荐配置而非附录内容。

**N3** [critical] 14B 实验严重混淆，"signal persists" claim 言过其实
- 具体位置：Section 5.4, Section 6 第 1 段, Appendix B.12 Table B.6 及 §Confounds
- 问题：14B 实验（Qwen2.5-14B, mean 50.8%, EDD=0）同时改变了 5 个变量：(a) model family（Qwen vs Pythia/OLMo/GPT-2）, (b) tokenizer, (c) training data, (d) reference model（self-reference vs cross-reference Pythia-1.4B）, (e) model scale（14B vs 1-1.5B）。Appendix B.12 §Confounds 承认 "it is therefore infeasible to attribute the observed accuracy gap to any single factor"，但 Section 5.4 和 Section 6 仍声称 "signal persists at 14B"。当 EDD=0（no adjacent-depth pair exceeds T=0.70）时，声称 "d1-d3 discrimination persists" 与 EDD 指标的定义矛盾——EDD 正是为了衡量这种 discrimination，而它报告为 0。50.8% 仅为 2× chance，在高方差小样本下可能不稳定。
- 为什么影响接收：这是 overclaiming。作者自己的 EDD 指标说 0，但结论说 "persists"，这是内部不一致。多重混淆使得无法将 50.8% 归因于 depth signal vs 其他因素。
- 建议修改方向：(1) 将 Section 5.4 标题从 "Preliminary Cross-Scale Observations" 改为更明确的 caveat（如 "Inconclusive Cross-Scale Observations"）；(2) Section 6 中不应使用 "persists"，改为 "above-chance accuracy is observed but cannot be attributed to depth signal due to multiple confounds"；(3) 在 14B 实验中加入 Qwen2.5-14B 的 Pythia-referenced pipeline（而非 self-reference）以隔离 reference model 混淆。

---

## Should-Fix 问题（影响评分但不一票否决）

**W1** [Should-Fix] Self-reference 混淆使 3×3 atlas 内部不可比
- 具体位置：Section 3.2 §Reference model, Table 2（†标注）, Appendix B.11 Table B.11
- 问题：Pythia-1.4B 同时作为 reference model 和 generator，self-reference 优势 4-11pp（Table B.11: self 78.6% vs cross-OLMo 74.5% vs cross-GPT2 67.3%）。这意味着 Table 2 中 Pythia 的 78.7% 可能在 cross-reference 下降至 ~68-75%，与 OLMo 和 GPT-2 XL 的表观优势关系反转。虽然论文用 † 标注并在 Limitations 中讨论，但 atlas 分析（Section 4）中的所有 cross-cell 比较（如 "GPT-2 XL achieves the highest accuracy under every strategy"）均基于这个不公平基础。
- 建议：在 Table 2 中增加一列 cross-reference accuracy（OLMo-1B 或 GPT-2 XL 作为 reference），使 atlas 内部比较基于相同条件。或者至少在 Section 4.1 的 axis effect 分析中明确说明 Pythia 行的可比性受限。

**W2** [Should-Fix] Cross-strategy transfer d1-d3 仅 45.9%（1.38× chance），实用性存疑
- 具体位置：Section 5.3 Table 6, Appendix B.23 §Cross-strategy conditional decomposition
- 问题：d1-d3 balanced accuracy 45.9%（chance 33.3%）意味着在 decoding strategy 未知时，系统对 generated text 的深度估计几乎没有实用价值。d1/d2 boundary inversion（AUC<0.5）意味着系统在某些 strategy 下会系统性地反转深度判断。Two-stage pipeline 回收 11.5pp，但前提是 strategy space 已知且 strategy classifier 准确——论文未报告 strategy classifier 本身的准确率。
- 建议：(1) 报告 two-stage pipeline 中 strategy classifier 的独立准确率；(2) 在 Section 6 中明确将 "decoding strategy must be known or identifiable" 列为部署前提条件，而非仅在 Limitations 中提及。

**W3** [Should-Fix] 单一 LoRA 超参配置（r=16, α=32）无 sensitivity analysis
- 具体位置：Section 3.2 §Generation pipeline, Appendix A Table A.1
- 问题：所有 180K 样本和全部实验使用相同 LoRA 配置。不同 LoRA rank（r=4, 8, 32, 64）和 learning rate 可能产生不同的 distributional shift patterns。如果 depth signal 部分来源于特定 LoRA rank 的 underfitting/overfitting 特征（r=16 可能比 full fine-tuning 产生更大的 distributional gap），那么结论的普适性受限。论文在 Limitations 中承认 "single LoRA instance" 但未提供任何 sensitivity analysis。
- 建议：至少在一个 model-strategy cell 上提供 r∈{4, 8, 16, 32} 的 sensitivity analysis，或与 full fine-tuning 对比一个 cell 的深度估计准确率。

**W4** [Should-Fix] Cross-seed replication 不充分（3/9 cells），OLMo +3.17pp 非重叠 CI 表明 benchmark 不稳定
- 具体位置：Appendix B.16 Table B.9
- 问题：仅 Pythia/OLMo/GPT-2 XL 的 nucleus cell 有 2-seed replication（3/9 cells）。OLMo seed=42 78.94% → seed=43 82.11%（+3.17pp），CI 不重叠。这意味着 Table 2 中的 OLMo nucleus accuracy 有 ~3pp 不确定性。温度和 top-k cells 完全未复制。更严重的是，feature rankings 的 seed stability 虽被声称 "identical top-3"，但未报告跨 seed 的 importance 值变化幅度。
- 建议：(1) 在所有 9 cells 上提供 cross-seed replication；(2) 报告 importance 值的 seed-wise 标准差。

**W5** [Should-Fix] EDD T=0.70 阈值选择缺乏充分依据
- 具体位置：Section 3.4, Section 4.3
- 问题：T=0.70 被选为 primary threshold，理由是 "corresponding to adequate discrimination in ROC analysis (8/9 cells achieve EDD ≥ 3)"。这是循环论证——选择一个让大多数 cells 看起来好的阈值。T=0.75 时只有 7/9 cells 达到 EDD≥3，T=0.80 时只有 5/9。论文确实报告了 sensitivity analysis（Section 4.3），但 T=0.70 的 "primary" 地位未基于外部标准（如 classification error rate bound, information-theoretic argument）论证。
- 建议：(1) 提供 T 选择的 principled justification（如与 downstream task performance 的关联，或与 classification error rate 的对应关系）；(2) 如无法提供，则在正文中将 T=0.70 定位为 "illustrative" 而非 "primary"。

**W6** [Should-Fix] Perturbation-based baselines 从 binary → ordinal 的适配不充分
- 具体位置：Section 5.1 Table 4, Appendix B.19
- 问题：DetectGPT（28.8%）和 Min-K% Prob（33.2%）是二分类方法，被改造为序数分类 baselines。DetectGPT 使用 "best-of-3" calibration，Min-K% 使用 CORAL calibration。但这些方法从未被设计用于序数深度估计——它们的 score 空间（perturbation discrepancy, token-level log-probability）不一定具有序数结构。28-33% 的性能接近 chance（25%），这可能反映适配方法的局限而非方法本身的局限。Appendix B.19 中 augmented feature set（19 + Min-K%）提升 +0.48pp 并 Min-K% 排名 #3，说明 Min-K% 确实携带互补信号——当配合合适的特征工程时可以工作。
- 建议：(1) 在 Table 4 中注明 "adapted from binary detection; comparison reflects ordinal adaptation rather than original method"；(2) 加入 min-K% 和 DetectGPT 的 binary d0-vs-d1+ 性能作为 sanity check。

**W7** [Should-Fix] Curation PoC（Appendix B.10）主结论非显著（p>0.4），存在多重比较问题
- 具体位置：Appendix B.10 Tables B.7 & B.8, Appendix B.23
- 问题：RF-filtered vs unfiltered（p=0.407）——主假设不成立。RF-vs-random 的 3 个 pairwise comparison（p<0.02 before Bonferroni）在 Bonferroni 校正后仅 1/3 存活（p<0.003 vs threshold 0.017）。论文在 Appendix B.23 中部分承认（"1 of 3 comparisons surviving"），但 Appendix B.10 的呈现未充分强调非显著的主结论。
- 建议：(1) 将 Appendix B.10 标题改为 "Curation PoC (Inconclusive)"；(2) 在正文中提及 curation 时使用 "inconclusive" 而非暗示有效。

---

## 小问题（不影响接收）

- **[Minor]** Table 4 中 Binoculars 的 calibration 列写 "threshold" 和 "RF (1 feat)"，但 78.1% 的 11-feat RF 配置未出现在 table 中。建议补充。
- **[Minor]** 引用验证：7 条在 OpenAlex 未找到（knowledge_collapse2025, falahati2026_curated, mitchell2023_detectgpt 等），多为 2025-2026 新论文或索引问题，非虚构。4 条有年份/first-author 微小 mismatch（he2021_deberta_v3 bib 标 2023 vs 实际 2021; alemohammad2024_mad first author mismatch）。建议修正 bib 年份。
- **[Minor]** Appendix B.12 中 7-8B 实验使用 4-bit NF4 QLoRA（与 1-1.5B 的 bf16 LoRA 不同），这一差异在 Table B.6 中未标注。
- **[Minor]** Section 5.1: "Single-feature regression on mean perplexity performs at chance (25.1%)" — 但 Table B.20 显示 p90_ppl alone 达到 58.3%。Mean perplexity 是最弱的 perplexity 特征，以它代表 "surface-text ablation" 可能低估了简单 baselines。
- **[Minor]** Cross-boundary generalization（Appendix B.15）：heterogeneous chain 的 confound（architecture identity ≡ depth）虽有 reverse-chain control，但 reverse chain 也只是将另一组 architecture 映射到 depth，无法完全排除 architecture fingerprint 的贡献。

---

## 主要优势

1. **问题定义新颖且有价值**：将递归生成深度估计形式化为序数分类问题，区别于现有的 binary human/machine detection，具有理论清晰性和实际意义。在 model collapse 文献中这是一个被忽视的逆问题。

2. **Benchmark 设计系统**：180K 样本覆盖 3 model families × 3 decoding strategies × 4 depths 的完整网格，控制变量严格（固定 LoRA 配置、固定 reference model、固定 seed text）。Domain bias analysis（Appendix B.8, Sub-A/B/C）包括 bug 修复透明披露，体现了实验诚信。

3. **EDD 指标有概念贡献**：将聚合准确率分解为逐深度边界的可判别性，提供了比单一准确率更有信息量的评估框架。虽然具体实现（contiguous prefix + fixed threshold）有改进空间，但概念方向正确。

4. **Feature analysis 深入且一致**：三种 importance measures（Gini, SHAP, permutation）的高一致性（Kendall's W=0.90, p<0.005），perplexity tail 特征在 9/9 cells 中的统治性，以及理论 grounding（tail erosion → decreasing p90_ppl）形成了完整的叙事。

5. **Limitations 异常全面**：论文用整整一页讨论了 10+ 个 limitations，包括 d0 inflation、FPR、self-reference confound、cross-strategy constraint 等。多数问题是作者自己识别并讨论的。这在 submission 中较为少见。

6. **Appendix 丰富**（15页附录，含 23 个子实验）：包括 domain bias 修正、calibration、feature overlap、end-to-end comparison、depth-4/5 extension、prompted generation、instruction-tuned model、cross-boundary chain 等。

---

## Missing References / Related Work

- **Recursive text generation detection**: 论文未引用 EditLens 之外的 partial-generation / mixed-origin detection 方法。虽然 depth estimation 是更窄的问题定义，但 sentence-level attribution 方法（如 SeqXGPT）与论文的 passage-level 假设形成对比，值得讨论。
- **Ordinal classification baselines**: 论文在 Appendix B.19 中比较了 CORAL、Frank & Hall、Rennie & Srebro 等 ordinal methods，但主文 Table 4 仅列 RF。建议在 Table 4 中加入 XGBoost（67.2%）和 Ordinal MLP（66.7%）的 cross-model transfer 结果以完整呈现 classifier 比较。

---

## Reviewer Confidence
4/5: 仔细阅读了 10 页正文 + 15 页附录的全部内容，核验了 EDD 定义的数学一致性、Table 2/4/5/6 的数值与 appendix 的对应关系、statistical tests 的使用（bootstrap CI, Wilson CI, paired t-test, Bonferroni correction）、以及 68 条引用的在线验证。对 model collapse 理论和 AI text detection 文献有一般性了解，但非该子领域核心研究者。

### 总体评分
**Overall**: 3.0 / 5（Findings 级别）
**一句话总结**: 任务定义新颖且实验设计系统，但方法贡献有限（标准 RF + 标准特征），scale generalization 在 14B 时崩塌（EDD=0），full-replacement 假设严重限制生态效度，综合来看达到 Findings 标准但不足以被主会议接收。

| 维度 | 分数 | 理由摘要 |
|------|------|----------|
| Soundness | 3.5/5 | 实验方法论严谨（5-fold CV, 多 seed, bootstrap CI），但 full-replacement 假设与 real-world accumulation 场景差距过大，14B 结果（EDD=0）与 "signal persists" 叙事存在张力 |

| Confidence | 4/5 | 熟悉 AI text detection 和 model collapse 文献 |

### Must-Fix 问题

**N1** [critical] Scale generalization 的叙事与证据之间存在系统性张力
- Abstract 声称 fingerprints "are consistent in direction but scale-dependent in magnitude"，但 14B 结果 EDD=0，4-class 准确率仅 50.8%（2× chance）。7-8B 优于 chance 但未重新训练分类器。在实际关心的模型规模（≥14B）上方法实用性未经验证。
- 建议：(1) Abstract 和 Introduction 中明确声明 14B EDD=0；(2) §5.4 扩展到主体正文；(3) 讨论 14B EDD=0 的可能原因及缓解方向。

**N2** [critical] Full-replacement 假设严重限制生态效度

- 建议：(1) 增加 partial-mixing 实验（50% synthetic + 50% real）；(2) 如无法实验，在 Discussion 中深入分析。

**N3** [critical] 算法贡献有限，论文定位需要更谨慎
- 核心方法是标准 RF + 19 个标准统计特征。所有特征在 detection 文献中已有广泛使用（GLTR, Ghostbuster 等）。DeBERTa-v3 端到端基线反而低于 RF。论文在 p.2 称 "our contribution centers on task formalization and systematic empirical characterization"，定位诚实，但 Findings 级别也需要 non-trivial 的方法论 insight。
- 建议：(1) 深入分析为什么 RF 大幅优于 neural 方法；(2) 加强 EDD 的 formalization 使其成为更有理论深度的贡献。

### Should-Fix 问题

**W1** Abstract 信息过载，核心信息被淹没
- Abstract 包含过多具体数字（"180K-passage", "three model families", "19 statistical features", 多个百分比），核心贡献被稀释。
- 建议：精简到 1-2 个 headline 数字。

**W2** Discussion 过于单薄，核心洞察被放逐到 Appendix
- §6 约 1 页，混合讨论和结论。关键分析（multi-channel encoding, RF vs neural, curation PoC, cross-scale）全在 Appendix。
- 建议：将 Appendix B.9 和 B.22 核心结论提升到主体。

**W3** "Depth Degradation Atlas" 作为概念贡献被过度包装
- "Atlas" 暗示全面参考地图，但实际是 3×3 grid 的 empirical evaluation。
- 建议：使用更准确术语如 "systematic empirical analysis"。

**W4** Cross-model 和 cross-strategy transfer 性能较弱但讨论不足
- 用户需要先知道是哪个模型、哪种解码策略才能选择正确分类器，限制 blind deployment 实用性。
- 建议：Discussion 增加 practical deployment constraints 分析。

**W5** Curation PoC 结果 inconclusive 但论文仍暗示为 contribution
- d0-only 非最低 PPL，单次实验缺乏统计显著性，但 §6 语气偏乐观。
- 建议：明确定调为 preliminary/inconclusive。

### Minor 问题
- M1: 部分 bib entry 年份不匹配（he2021_deberta_v3, alemohammad2024_mad, guo2024_biscope）
- M2: gerstgrasser2024_accumulate 和 briesch2024selfconsuming 应更新为 inproceedings
- M3: AI 写作痕迹（-ing 分词短语多处出现）

## Reviewer 1 交叉回应 — 对 Reviewer 2（新颖性与完整性）审稿意见的逐条回应

---

### 总体评分
[AGREE] R2 的 Overall 3.0 (Findings) 评分。我给出了相同分数，理由高度重叠：任务定义新颖、benchmark 系统，但方法贡献有限、scale generalization 不足、cross-transfer 实用性存疑。

---

### Must-Fix 问题

**[AGREE] R2-N1: Scale generalization 叙事与证据的系统性张力**

完全同意。我在自己的 N3 中提出了本质相同的问题。补充两点 R2 未明确提到的证据：

(1) 14B 实验的内部不一致更深层：论文自己定义的 EDD 指标（Section 3.4 Definition 1）在 14B 上报告 EDD=0，这意味着按照论文自己的度量标准，14B 文本的相邻深度不可判别。但 Section 6 第 1 段仍写 "d1-d3 discrimination persists with strategy-specific AUC patterns"——这与 EDD=0 的定义矛盾。

(2) Table B.6 中 14B 的 d0v1 AUC（0.561-0.643）远低于 1-1.5B 的 >0.99。考虑到 d0/d1 boundary 是整个框架中最容易的判别（human vs first-gen），这个 boundary 的崩塌比 d1-d3 的困难更值得关注——它暗示 14B 的 depth signal 可能根本是不同性质的，而非同一信号的 scale-dependent attenuation。

**[REBUT] R2-N2: Full-replacement 假设严重限制生态效度 → 不同意 "critical" 严重度**

R2 将此标为 critical，我认为应降为 Should-Fix，理由如下：

(1) Full-replacement 是研究递归生成深度的 *必要起点*。正如 controlled experiment 需要隔离变量，full-replacement 消除了 mixing ratio 这个连续混淆变量，使 depth 成为唯一自变量。论文明确声明 "Our results therefore represent an upper bound on feature separability"（Limitations §1），定位为 upper bound 而非 real-world deployment 方案。

(2) Gerstgrasser et al. (2024) 证明 accumulation 可避免 collapse，但这恰恰说明 full-replacement 场景下 depth signal 更强——论文选择 signal 最强的设定来建立 feasibility，再逐步推广，是合理的研究策略。

(3) 论文已有 partial evidence：prompted generation（Appendix B.22, Table B.15: 69.5%, -13.8pp）和 mixed-depth corpus（Appendix B.14: macro-recall Δ=-1.62pp）提供了部分 relaxation。完整的 accumulation 实验确实重要，但其缺失不构成对当前贡献的否定——它是 future work，不是 fatal flaw。

(4) 作为 Findings 论文，在 controlled setting 下建立 feasibility + 系统实证分析已足够。要求 accumulation 实验等同于要求一篇论文同时解决 controlled 和 wild 场景。

建议维持 Should-Fix：在 Discussion 中加深 accumulation 场景的分析，但不需要新实验。

**[AGREE with nuance] R2-N3: 算法贡献有限**

同意 R2 的判断，但有细微差异：

(1) 同意 "RF + 19 标准特征" 本身无算法创新。但 R2 声称 "所有特征在 detection 文献中已有广泛使用（GLTR, Ghostbuster 等）" 不完全准确。GLTR 和 Ghostbuster 使用的是 token-level log-probability 和 per-token rank 特征，而本文的 *passage-level distributional statistics*（p90_ppl, var_surprisal, kurtosis_ppl）是对 token-level 信号的 distributional aggregation——这是一个非 trivial 的特征工程选择，并且论文展示了为什么这种 aggregation 有效（tail erosion 理论，Section 3.5）而 token-level 方法（DetectGPT 28.8%, Min-K% 33.2%）失败。

(2) 同意 EDD 的 formalization 有改进空间。当前定义（Definition 1, Section 3.4）的 contiguous prefix 要求在 non-monotonic 场景下过于保守（如论文自己在 Limitations 中承认）。如果 EDD 能处理 non-contiguous discriminable regions，将显著增强理论贡献。

(3) R2 建议 "深入分析为什么 RF 大幅优于 neural 方法" ——我强烈支持。论文有 partial 分析（Appendix B.7 feature overlap analysis: PLM [CLS] representations yield negative R² for var_surprisal and p90_ppl），但这个结果非常有趣且未在主文中充分展开。如果加强为 "perplexity tail statistics are not linearly accessible in pretrained representation space"，这可以成为一个有价值的 insight。

---

### Should-Fix 问题

**[REBUT] R2-W1: Abstract 信息过载**

不同意。ACL/EMNLP 的 abstract 惯例允许甚至鼓励包含具体数字以便检索和快速评估。我审查的 abstract 中的 key numbers（180K, 3 model families, 59-82%, 9-cell grid）每个都 serve a specific purpose：benchmark scale, generalization scope, performance range, experimental design。问题不在于数字过多，而在于 *which* numbers are highlighted——正如我在 N1 中指出，d1-d3 balanced accuracy 应与 four-class accuracy 并列呈现，而非用 four-class 单独 headline。

**[AGREE] R2-W2: Discussion 过于单薄**

同意。Section 6 约 1 页，混合了 summary 和 discussion。关键分析（multi-channel encoding 分解、RF vs neural 的 representational gap、cross-scale 趋势的 theoretical implications）全在 Appendix。建议将 Appendix B.7（feature overlap analysis）和 B.17（Binoculars signal decomposition）的核心结论提升到 Section 6，使 discussion 更有理论深度。

**[REBUT] R2-W3: "Depth Degradation Atlas" 过度包装**

不完全同意。"Atlas" 在计量学和系统生物学中指 systematic empirical map across a parameter grid——论文的 3 model families × 3 strategies × 4 depths × 19 features 的系统性评估，加上跨维度的 consistency analysis（feature rank correlation ρ̄=0.868, Table 3）和 sensitivity analysis（EDD at multiple thresholds），符合 "atlas" 的使用惯例。如果只是单一模型的 accuracy table，称 "atlas" 确实过度；但 9 cells 的完整交叉分析 + feature trajectory + EDD decay curve + importance heatmap（Figure 1）构成了一个有参考价值的 empirical map。

不过 R2 说 "暗示全面参考地图" 有道理——3×3 grid 的覆盖范围确实有限（3 个 model families 均为 1-1.5B，且仅 nucleus/temp/top-k 三种 strategy）。建议折中：保留 "atlas" 但在首次使用时加注 scope（"a 3×3 atlas at the 1-1.5B scale"）。

**[AGREE] R2-W4: Cross-model 和 cross-strategy transfer 性能较弱但讨论不足**

同意。我在 W2 中提出了类似问题。补充一个 R2 未明确提到的点：two-stage pipeline（strategy identification + depth classification）回收 11.5pp，但论文未报告 strategy classifier 本身的准确率。如果 strategy identification 本身不可靠，two-stage pipeline 的实际增益会打折扣。这是 deployment feasibility 的关键缺失。

**[AGREE] R2-W5: Curation PoC 结果 inconclusive 但论文仍暗示为 contribution**

完全同意。我在 W7 中提出了相同问题。RF-vs-unfiltered p=0.407，主假设不成立。Bonferroni 校正后仅 1/3 RF-vs-random comparisons 存活（Appendix B.23 自己承认）。Section 6 和 Appendix B.23 的措辞（"inconclusive preliminary evidence"）已比早期版本改善，但 Appendix B.10 的标题（"Downstream Curation PoC"）和呈现方式仍可能给 skimming reader 留下 positive 印象。

---

### Minor 问题

**[AGREE] R2-M1**: bib 年份不匹配。我在引用验证中也发现了相同问题（he2021_deberta_v3: bib=2023 vs actual=2021; alemohammad2024_mad: first author mismatch; guo2024_biscope: first author mismatch）。

**[AGREE] R2-M2**: gerstgrasser2024_accumulate 等应从 misc 更新为 inproceedings（如已被会议接收）。

**[REBUT] R2-M3: AI 写作痕迹（-ing 分词短语）**

不同意将此列为问题。-ing participial phrases 是学术英语中的标准构造（如 "confirming that...", "suggesting that...", "indicating that..."），在 NLP/ML 论文中普遍使用。Ethics Statement 透明披露了 "This research used AI coding assistants for experiment implementation and writing drafts"（p.10）。除非 R2 能指出具体的不自然表述，仅以 -ing 频率为由标记 "AI 写作痕迹" 缺乏依据，且与 double-blind review 的精神相悖（不应基于写作风格推断作者身份或工具使用）。

**[AGREE] R2-M4**: Figure 1 heatmap 对比度有限。从 PDF 视觉检查来看，低 importance 值之间的颜色区分确实不够明显。

**[AGREE] R2-M5**: 脚注 1 中 EDD binary classifier 使用 500 trees vs main 4-class RF 200 trees，未解释原因。这是一个合理的实验设计问题——不同 tree 数量可能影响 AUC 估计，且 EDD 的 AUC 阈值判定对 classifier capacity 敏感。

---

### Claim-Evidence 匹配分析

[AGREE] R2 的所有 6 条 claim-evidence 匹配判断。特别强调：

- "signal persists at larger scales" ⚠️：这与我的 N3 一致。50.8% (2× chance) 在 5 个混淆变量下不能归因于 depth signal。
- "curation PoC" ⚠️：p>0.4 的主假设检验不成立，应明确标记为 inconclusive。

---

### 可能遗漏的相关工作

**[AGREE]** R2 建议补充的 4 篇参考文献均有道理：
1. PAN 2026 (Generative Plagiarism Detection) — 如果确实存在该 shared task，直接相关
